name: Code the Dream
description: Code the Dream expands access to tech careers for individuals from underrepresented communities through free coding education and paid apprenticeships. By combining training with real-world experience, the program builds skills, creates opportunity, and delivers technology that benefits communities.

name: Student U
description: Student U is a Durham-based nonprofit working to create a more equitable education system by supporting students facing systemic barriers. Through long-term academic and college-access support, Student U helps students reach their full potential.

name: Youth LEAD NC
description: Youth LEAD NC is a nonprofit that empowers individuals with disabilities ages 30 and under through peer support and leadership development, preparing them to succeed in education, employment, independent living, and community leadership.

name: North Carolina Civics Coalition (NC3)
description: The North Carolina Civics Coalition (NC3) is a nonpartisan organization dedicated to strengthening and advancing K–12 civic education across North Carolina.

name: Pasquines Volunteer and Internship Program
description: Pasquines offers flexible volunteer and internship opportunities with a nonprofit news organization covering U.S. territories, allowing participants to build skills through remote, tech-driven collaboration. Requiring as little as two hours per week, it is ideal for students interested in journalism, public administration, political science, and law who want to gain experience while making an impact.

name: Teens In Public Service (TIPS) Internship
description: Teens In Public Service (TIPS) offers paid summer internships that place high school students with nonprofit organizations to make a meaningful impact in their communities. The program helps teens gain real-world experience while developing leadership skills and a strong sense of civic responsibility.

name: Arts Access
description: Arts Access is an organization that supports individuals with disabilities in accessing and participating in the arts. Volunteers can contribute skills in marketing and graphic design to help expand outreach and increase community engagement. It is a meaningful opportunity to support inclusivity while applying creative skills.

name: A Place at the Table
description: This welcoming downtown café builds community by serving fresh, delicious meals to everyone, regardless of their ability to pay. Guests can support others by adding a token to their bill to help cover someone else’s meal. It is a meaningful place to enjoy good food while giving back.

name: Communities in Schools of Wake County
description: This program supports students in staying in school and graduating by connecting them with mentors and community resources. Volunteers can get involved as youth mentors or assist in after school centers to provide guidance and support. It is a meaningful way to help students succeed academically and personally.

name: Designed for Joy
description: This studio on Crabtree Boulevard creates stylish leather earrings while providing meaningful employment for women in transitional situations. It offers a living wage, work experience, and professional references to help participants move forward in the job market. Supporting the studio, in person or online, helps empower women through opportunity and skill building.

name: Dorcas Ministries
description: Dorcas Ministries provides emergency support such as food, clothing, shelter, transportation, and other essential services to those in need. They are currently seeking grocery store gift cards to support clients of their food pantry. Donating is a direct way to help families facing immediate challenges.

name: Families Together
description: Families Together helps families experiencing homelessness secure stable housing and connect with essential community resources. Supporters can get involved by joining the Landlord Network, creating welcome baskets, or providing gifts for families during the holidays. It is a meaningful way to help families rebuild stability and independence.

name: Friends of Wake County Animal Center
description: FWCAC supports animals in the community by funding medical care, organizing supply drives, and facilitating fostering and adoption. Volunteers can contribute by using photography skills for adoption listings or fostering pets during the holidays. It is a meaningful way to improve the lives of animals while supporting their journey to permanent homes.

name: The Green Chair Project
description: Green Chair helps families recovering from homelessness, crisis, or disaster by providing essential home furnishings to create a sense of comfort and stability. Supporters can donate gently used furniture or new, gender neutral twin sized bedding to help furnish homes for those in need. It is a direct way to help local families rebuild and feel at home again.

name: Haven House Services
description: Haven House supports youth experiencing homelessness or crisis through a range of programs, including an emergency shelter for ages 10 to 17. Community members can get involved by adopting a family and providing holiday gifts to brighten a young person’s season. It is a meaningful way to support vulnerable youth and bring comfort during difficult times.

name: Helping Horse
description: This therapeutic riding program provides group lessons for individuals with physical, mental, and emotional needs, helping build coordination and confidence. Supporters can donate new or gently used equipment such as saddles, bridles, and grooming tools. It is a meaningful way to promote healing and empowerment through equine therapy.

name: Inter-Faith Food Shuttle
description: The Food Shuttle works to combat hunger by providing food access and community support programs. Volunteers can lead health education classes, organize food drives, or support initiatives like Backpack Buddies at local schools. It offers multiple ways to make a direct impact on food insecurity in the community.

name: Kid Lab
description: This downtown nonprofit makerspace and community art collective offers pay what you can, play based creative experiences for all ages. Donating art supplies helps expand access and inspire creativity in more kids and families. It is a great way to support inclusive, hands on learning in the community.

name: Lutheran Family Services Resettlement Help
description: LFS supports refugees and immigrants by helping them secure housing, access healthcare, and enroll in school. Community members can join a “Circle of Welcome” or donate essential household items like tea kettles and rice cookers. It is a meaningful way to help families settle in and build a new life.

name: Me Fine Foundation
description: Me Fine supports families with critically ill children by providing financial and emotional assistance so they can focus on their child’s care. Donating gas cards helps families travel to important medical appointments and follow ups. It is a simple but meaningful way to ease both financial and emotional burdens.

name: NC Hunters for the Hungry
description: Licensed hunters can donate legally harvested deer, which are processed at state inspected facilities and turned into nutritious venison for those in need. The program helps manage deer overpopulation in North Carolina while providing high quality protein to people experiencing hunger. It is a unique way to support both environmental balance and food access.

name: Note in the Pocket
description: Note in the Pocket supports children in poverty by providing high quality clothing that helps them feel confident and succeed in school. Donations of new or gently used clothing in sizes 5T through adult help meet the needs of students of all ages. It is a meaningful way to support both dignity and academic success.

name: Oak City Cares
description: This community hub works to make homelessness rare, brief, and non recurring by providing essential services like meals, showers, laundry, medical screenings, and computer access. Volunteers can help by serving meals or assisting at the front desk. It is a direct way to support individuals working toward stability and independence.

name: Oak City Recovery Run Club
description: At OCRRC, the Raleigh running community comes together with individuals in recovery through regular group runs, helping reduce the stigma around addiction. Participants can join 1, 3, or 5 mile runs or donate winter running gear to support the program. It is a powerful way to build community, promote wellness, and support recovery.

name: Raleigh Community Kickstand
description: This bicycle cooperative repairs donated bikes, teaches maintenance skills, and provides bicycles to unhoused neighbors to support reliable transportation. Community members can donate adult sized bikes or offer space for pop up workshops. It is a practical way to promote mobility, skill building, and community support.

name: Read and Feed
description: Read and Feed supports elementary students by combining after school literacy tutoring with nutritious meals. Donating diverse K to 5 books or gas cards helps expand access to their mobile classroom and resources. It is a meaningful way to support both education and food security for children.

name: SAFEChild
description: SAFEChild works to prevent child abuse and support families through education, advocacy, and parent to parent programs. Volunteers can mentor new mothers, lead children’s groups, or donate items from their wish list. It is a meaningful way to strengthen families and create safer environments for children.

name: StepUp Ministry
description: StepUp helps individuals find employment, build life skills, and create stability within a supportive community. Donating large sized professional men’s clothing helps stock their winter closet and prepares participants for job opportunities. It is a practical way to support confidence and long term success.

name: Triangle Land Conservancy
description: TLC works to preserve natural spaces and connect people with nature in a rapidly developing region. Volunteers can help prepare new nature preserves or support efforts by donating vehicles for work days. It is a meaningful way to protect the environment and expand access to outdoor spaces.

name: Urban Ministries
description: Urban Ministries supports individuals facing crisis or poverty by providing food, medicine, and shelter with compassion and dignity. Donations of clothing like T shirts, yoga pants, socks, and underwear help women at the Helen Wright Center meet basic needs. It is a direct way to offer comfort and support during difficult times.

name: Mountains to Sea Trail
description: Betsy Brown from the Mountains to Sea Trail is a helpful contact for coordinating volunteer efforts related to trail work along the Eno River. Due to natural erosion, some sections of the trail need to be rerouted, creating opportunities for hands on service. Volunteers should come prepared with appropriate clothing, gloves, and water for outdoor work.

name: Eartheal
description: Eartheal is a 4 acre site near Duke Forest where volunteers help maintain and improve outdoor learning spaces. Projects may include clearing trails, spreading gravel, light carpentry, and creating signs. Those interested in volunteering can reach out to Jane for more information and coordination.

name: Durham Public/Private Schools
description: Volunteering with local schools is a great way to give back through hands on projects like outdoor maintenance and creative painting. Schools such as EK Powe Elementary, Creekside Elementary, Immaculata Catholic School, and Bethesda Elementary welcome support for improving their spaces. Reaching out directly to school offices is an effective way to coordinate and get involved.

name: Animal Protection Society
description: APS offers on site volunteer opportunities at their shelter throughout the week, with Saturdays being especially busy for community outreach and education. Volunteers can support animal care and engagement efforts in a hands on environment. Annika Hugosson is a helpful contact for coordinating involvement and learning more about opportunities.

name: Goodwill Community Foundation (GCF) Global
description: GCF Global offers volunteer opportunities at their Durham site, where participants help with tasks like planting, cultivating, and harvesting produce that is donated to local food banks and nonprofits. Volunteers can also assist with indoor projects such as jewelry processing, electronics recycling, and assembling school kits. They request a 24 hour notice before volunteering, and Huong Hornshuh is a helpful contact for coordination.

name: Housing for New Hope
description: Housing for New Hope works to prevent and end homelessness by providing housing, healthcare, and integrated support services. Community members can get involved or learn more by reaching out through their email or phone. It is an impactful organization focused on helping individuals achieve long term stability.

name: Durham Rescue Mission
description: Durham Rescue Mission serves the greater Durham community through a wide range of volunteer opportunities, including meal service, tutoring, thrift store support, landscaping, and helping with donation drives. Even if scheduling does not always align, there are many flexible ways to get involved and give back. Those interested can contact the organization directly by email or phone to coordinate volunteering.

name: Scrap Exchange
description: The Scrap Exchange promotes creativity and environmental awareness by encouraging reuse and reducing waste within the community. They offer both group and individual volunteer opportunities, making it easy to get involved at any scale. It is a great way to support sustainability while engaging in creative, community focused work.

name: Triangle Land Conservancy
description: The Triangle Land Conservancy works to protect natural habitats while fostering community collaboration through conservation efforts. Volunteers can contribute through outdoor projects like trail maintenance and education, or support office based work. It offers a meaningful way to get involved in environmental protection and community engagement.

name: Durham Center for Senior Life
description: The Durham Center for Senior Life supports older adults through programs focused on education, recreation, nutrition, and social services. Volunteers can assist with projects such as administrative tasks to help the organization run smoothly. It is a meaningful way to support and engage with the senior community.

name: ReStore
description: ReStore sells gently used furniture, household goods, and building materials to support Habitat for Humanity’s mission. Volunteers can get involved by helping with store operations and organizing donations. It is a practical way to promote reuse while contributing to affordable housing efforts.

name: The Salvation Army
description: The Salvation Army supports the community through programs like weekly Free Food Friday and an affordable family thrift store. Volunteers can help distribute food or assist with store operations, making it easy to get involved. It is a meaningful way to support families in need while giving back locally.

name: East Durham Children’s Initiative
description: The East Durham Children’s Initiative supports children from early childhood through high school graduation by providing programs and community support. Volunteers can get involved in activities like community cleanups or other family focused initiatives. It is a meaningful way to contribute to long term student success and community development.

name: Ronald McDonald House of Durham
description: The Ronald McDonald House of Durham supports families with children receiving medical care through a range of services and volunteer opportunities. Individuals and groups can help by cooking meals, donating items, or assisting with in hospital and child focused activities. It is a meaningful way to provide comfort and support to families during challenging times.

name: United Way
description: United Way of the Greater Triangle addresses key community needs such as homelessness, hunger, education, and career readiness. The organization has invested millions of dollars into local programs and agencies to create lasting impact. It offers meaningful ways to get involved in supporting broad community initiatives.

name: Durham Central Park
description: Durham Central Park offers volunteer opportunities such as monthly cleanups for paths and gardens, as well as support for events like Food Truck Rodeos. They can also accommodate large group volunteer projects. It is an accessible way to help maintain and energize a shared community space.

name: TROSA
description: TROSA supports its residential recovery program through a thrift and donation store, with all proceeds going toward helping its residents. Volunteers can assist by sorting and processing donations, directly contributing to the organization’s mission. It is a meaningful way to support recovery and community reintegration.

name: Sandy Creek Park
description: Sandy Creek Park, once a wastewater treatment site, has been transformed into a thriving natural habitat and community space. The park offers opportunities for large group volunteer events focused on environmental restoration and maintenance. Getting involved is simple through their online contact form, making it an accessible way to support local conservation efforts.

name: Veterans at Maple Court
description: Maple Court supports homeless veterans by helping them transition into stable housing and rebuild their lives. Volunteers can get involved by providing meals or organizing activities like game nights to build community. It is a meaningful way to support and connect with veterans in the local area.

name: Black Farmers' Market
description: A nonprofit dedicated to building healthier communities while empowering Black farmers and entrepreneurs. Its work focuses on fostering economic growth and sustainability within these communities.

name: Caring House
description: Caring House supports patients at Duke Cancer Institute by offering affordable housing, a healing environment, and a welcoming, supportive community that brings peace of mind.

name: Book Harvest
description: Since 2011, Book Harvest has distributed more than 2.2 million books to families, equipping parents with the resources to support and nurture their children’s literacy.

name: Carolina Small Business Development Fund
description: The Carolina Small Business Development Fund is a statewide nonprofit CDFI that supports small businesses through access to capital, technical assistance, and policy research.

name: Child Care Services Association
description: Early Years is a nationally recognized nonprofit dedicated to expanding access to affordable, high-quality child care for all families through research, services, and advocacy.

name: Durham Art Guild
description: Durham Art Guild fosters connection and community through the power of art.

name: Durham Arts Council, Inc.
description: The Durham Arts Council is a private nonprofit that drives Durham’s cultural growth by offering leadership, advocacy, programming, and support for artists and arts organizations.

name: Durham TRY/Pinnacle Community Development Corporation
description: TRY works to improve community health by addressing the root causes of issues like substance use, violence, mental health challenges, and food insecurity through a public health and socio-ecological approach. It focuses on building resilience, reducing risk, and driving equitable change through advocacy, community engagement, and collective action.

name: Durham's Partnership For Children, Inc.
description: This organization works to ensure every child in Durham is ready for school by supporting children from birth to age five and their families. It promotes healthy development and expands access to high-quality early care and learning.

name: Emily Krzyzewski Center
description: The Emily Krzyzewski Center is a Durham-based nonprofit that supports students traditionally underrepresented in higher education through programs focused on academics, careers, and leadership. Serving students from elementary school through college, it equips them with the skills to succeed in higher education, pursue meaningful careers, and create positive change in their communities.

name: Elna B. Spaulding Conflict Resolution Center
description: This nonprofit conflict resolution center empowers individuals and communities to address conflict constructively through mediation, training, and restorative practices. By fostering respectful dialogue and inclusive spaces, it helps people feel heard and move forward together.

name: Families and Communities Rising
description: The organization envisions a community where children, families, educators, and communities reach their full potential and embrace lifelong learning. Its mission is to educate and empower through innovative educational programs and supportive services.

name: Eno River Association
description: The Eno River Association is an accredited land trust dedicated to conserving and protecting the natural, historical, and cultural resources of the Eno River basin.

name: Farmer Foodshare
description: Farmer Foodshare is a Triangle-based food hub that works to expand access to fresh, local food while supporting marginalized North Carolina farmers and building a more equitable food system.

name: Family Promise of the Triangle
description: Family Promise of the Triangle is a nonprofit that has supported families facing or at risk of temporary homelessness in Durham and Wake Counties for over 30 years.
